To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fishers' memories can be used as a valuable tool to complement available data and characterise historical fishing activity and exploited marine ecosystems.
fishers' perceptions can be used to assess changes in fishing activity, and to document local ecological changes in marine ecosystems.

(1) fishing activity has substantially expanded towards deeper grounds and distant areas; (2) fishers have documented declines and local extirpations of several commercially important fish and shellfish, in line with quantitative information; (3) fishers have also documented proliferations of some species that could be related to climate change effects and trophic cascading effects due to fishing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the need to integrate different types of data to understand and monitor changes in marine ecosystems.
the need to integrate qualitative and quantitative information to better evaluate the effects of anthropogenic activities and climate change in the marine environment.
the need for more information on the history of fisheries and marine ecosystems to better understand the present and future state of marine ecosystems and fisheries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

fishing activity and marine biodiversity substantially changed in the Spanish Mediterranean and Gulf area, with declines and extirpation of commercially exploited species and local ecological changes, such as trophic cascading effects.

fishing activity and marine biodiversity have substantially changed in the study area over the last half of century, with fishing activity expanding towards deeper grounds, towards more distant areas and with a substantial decrease of the maximum catches ever recorded and of the size of the largest species captured.
the fishing activity and the exploited ecosystems have substantially changed in the Spanish Mediterranean and Gulf area during the last 40 years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fishers' perceptions provide a valuable tool to assess fishing and marine biodiversity changes, and can be used to complement available data and to improve management and conservation actions.
fishers' perceptions can be used to assess fishing and biodiversity changes.
fishers' perceptions can help to understand changes in marine ecosystems, and that this approach can be used in areas where data are scarce.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of fishers' knowledge with quantitative data can help to better understand the evolution of fishing activities and the changes in marine biodiversity.
fishers are a rich source of information about the past and the present of marine ecosystems.
fishers' knowledge and experience should be included in the management and conservation of marine resources and ecosystems.
